claims.text: High mixing entropy predicts intrinsic thermal stability in nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
Surface-energy minimization overrides entropy-based stabilization in these nanoparticles.
Rapid atomic diffusion at elevated temperature overrides entropy-based stabilization in these nanoparticles.
Elevated-temperature exposure causes premature separation into ordered intermetallics or elementally segregated regions.
Lattice distortion kinetically stabilizes the solid solution in bulk high-entropy alloys.
Sluggish diffusion kinetically stabilizes the solid solution in bulk high-entropy alloys.
CoNiCrFeMn and NbMoTaW are examples of nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal alloy systems.
The proposed starting nanoparticles possess a single-phase FCC or BCC solid-solution structure.
Bulk alloys typically maintain stability during extended annealing at 600–1000 °C.
Particle diameters below 50 nm maximize surface-to-volume effects.
A high surface-to-volume ratio accelerates atomic diffusion relative to bulk material.
High grain-boundary density accelerates atomic diffusion relative to bulk material.
High surface-to-volume ratio and grain-boundary density lower the nucleation barrier for phase separation.
High nanoparticle surface energy produces a thermodynamic instability of the single-phase solid solution.
Lower-energy L12 or B2 ordered phases, or elemental segregation, are favored over the nanoparticle solid solution.
Nanoparticle surface effects bypass the kinetic barriers that protect bulk high-entropy alloys.
Nanoparticles decompose at temperatures significantly below the decomposition temperature of the corresponding bulk alloy.
Bulk alloys of the same composition retain a single-phase solid solution up to near-melting temperatures.
The instability mechanism applies below 50 nm but may fail above 100 nm because surface effects become negligible.
The decomposition threshold depends on the transition-metal combination and particle-size distribution.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is framed around five-transition-metal nanoparticles, but NbMoTaW, one of the stated examples, contains only four elements.
